speaker: Brenda Okoro
cascadeSummary: The Fund's charter renewal goes to council this cycle with the business-and-resident scope, the 23-day standard, and the published closeout evidence intact, and I'm announcing no new tranche — renewal is council's to call, not mine to declare. I'm holding the Grand Lake line at YES on the recorded full-council vote with every Chen-Vega milestone and audit condition attached, and claiming no outcome before the roll exists. And I'm responding to the sour blocks — Brooklyn, Ivy Hill, San Antonio, Laurel — with the same feet-on-the-ground answer I gave last cycle, not a citywide press line.

statements.topic: West Oakland Stabilization Fund — charter renewal goes to council this cycle
statements.decision: ACT — Call for council consideration of the transmitted charter-renewal ordinance with business-and-resident scope, the 23-day processing standard, and the C114 closeout evidence intact; announce no new tranche this cycle.
statements.quote: The renewal ordinance is on the table with the scope that works — businesses and residents both eligible, 23 days processing, every closeout record public. I'm not announcing a new tranche, because renewal is council's call to make and my job is to make the record clean enough for them to make it.
statements.fullStatement: The West Oakland Stabilization Fund's charter renewal goes to council this cycle. I'm calling for that consideration with the ordinance exactly as translated: business-and-resident scope intact, the 23-day processing standard intact, and the C114 closeout publication publicly available for scrutiny. What I am not doing is announcing a new tranche. Renewal is council's call — I said that last cycle and I'll say it again, because the Fund earns its renewal through delivered support and documented records, not through me calling it early. The standard holds. The scope holds. The record is public. Council takes it from here.

statements.topic: Commercial Stabilization for Grand Lake — recorded full-council vote
statements.decision: ACT — Maintain a YES position and request the recorded full-council vote this cycle with all Chen-Vega milestone and audit conditions intact; claim no outcome before the roll exists.
statements.quote: Public money deserves public proof. Grand Lake gets the $2.5 million with every Chen-Vega milestone and audit condition attached, and every councilmember on the record — no hearing statement counted as a vote.
statements.fullStatement: Grand Lake's commercial stabilization is due for a recorded full-council vote this cycle. My position does not move: yes, with every Chen-Vega milestone and audit condition attached, exactly as referred and advanced through the committee. What I want is a roll — a yes-or-no the neighborhood can read. A hearing statement is not a vote, and I won't claim an outcome before the roll exists. The $2.5 million comes with public proof attached, or it doesn't come.

statements.topic: Where the work goes next — Ivy Hill, Brooklyn, San Antonio, Laurel
statements.decision: ACT — Direct field follow-through to the soured-trade and slow-trade blocks (Ivy Hill, Brooklyn, San Antonio, Laurel) as the cycle's community-development priority, with the Glenview and Piedmont Ave medium-severity spikes placed on the executive follow-up agenda through the responsible offices.
statements.quote: Oakland isn't one mood. Ivy Hill, Brooklyn, San Antonio, Laurel — those are the blocks still hurting, and we answer with feet on the ground, not a citywide press line. A quiet week across town is not permission to ignore what's loud on four blocks.
statements.fullStatement: The city reads quiet this cycle — most districts upbeat, trade busy, crime low. That's true and it's not the whole picture. Ivy Hill and Brooklyn are still soured. San Antonio and Laurel still have slow trade. Those are the blocks the work goes to, and the answer is the same one I gave last cycle: feet on the ground, block by block, not a citywide press line papering over the difference. Separately, the medium-severity spikes in Glenview and Piedmont Ave go on the executive follow-up agenda with a responsible office and a next public update before anyone closes them. A quiet week across town is not permission to ignore a spike or a soured mood — and it's not permission to ignore the neighbors building Oakland's civic life on these blocks either.
